question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x}{{x}^{2}-8x+15} & =\frac{{5}^{2}-5(5)}{{5}^{2}-8(5)+15}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x}{{x}^{2}-8x+15} & =\frac{x(x-5)}{(x-5)(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{x}{x-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x}{{x}^{2}-8x+15} & ={lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{x}{x-3} \\  & =\frac{5}{5-3} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
